body: **On hold (contributor, 2026-11-09):** no agent works the SolidCraft UI changes (#655 and its sub-issues #658, #659, #661) until the maintainer has reviewed and signed off on the direction. Please don't pick or claim this until then. The maintainer may mark it `P?` (paused).

## Estimate and proposed breakdown (agent, for the maintainer, 2026-11-12)

**Verdict:** `effort:high`; 5-6 PRs after one preparation PR; roughly 2-3k changed lines, about half of them deletions. It is blocked twice: on #658, and on SolidCraft's written permission, because **`solidcraft-theme` is no longer Apache-2.0**. This is a read-only estimate: nothing was built, filed, labelled or claimed.

### Corrections to the issue text (checked today on SolidCraft `main`, `9fd103a0f3`)
- **Licence.** Since 2026-11-10 14:06 UTC (their commit `312454f899`) `solidcraft-theme` is under the "SolidCraft Brand and Interface Licence" (`license-file = "LICENSE"`). Its clause 1c names "the design tokens, colour palettes, accent ramps, sizes and spacing"; clause 3a asks for the maintainers' written permission before "linking to the UI kit, the look or the theme from software that is not SolidCraft". The plan line "Apache-2.0, keep the NOTICE" no longer holds. Details are in the estimate on #655.
- **`solidcraft-color`** is still MIT OR Apache-2.0, but it is 140 lines (the sRGB transfer function and an analysis palette). There is no look in it.
- **Pin form.** Neither crate is on crates.io (both answer 404). The pin is a git `rev` of the SolidCraft repository, which is a 521 MB clone.
- **Light dependencies.** `solidcraft-theme` needs only `egui`, `serde`, `serde_json` and `solidcraft-color`: no patched egui-wgpu and no kernel crates. This is the cheap part of #655 to build.
- **No theme files in it.** The theme crate knows no theme-file format; that lives in `solidcraft-ui-kit` (`theme_files.rs`). So our theme files are not settled by this issue alone.

### What the work is (our side, measured)
- **Tokens.** `theme.rs` (402 lines) holds one `Tokens` struct with 31 fields in two columns (dark, light) and builds `egui::Visuals` from it. 233 token references in 49 files read our field names. SolidCraft's `Tokens` is far larger (its `lib.rs` is 90 KB), so each of our 31 has to be mapped, and some will have no counterpart.
- **Colour vision.** `colorvision.rs` (377), `cvd.rs` (174) and `colorvision_tests.rs` (167), with 70 references in 26 files. Our layer remaps CAM meanings: the verdict classes (clean, rest, gouge, unjudged), the move kinds (feed, rapid, plunge), selection and warning inks. SolidCraft's `ColorVision` knows CAD meanings. The modes can map across; the verdict palette and its separation gate must stay ours.
- **Our theme files.** `theme_files.rs` (456), `theme_dir.rs` (200), `theme_drop.rs` (149), `contrast.rs` (172), `tests/theme_files.rs` (362), `assets/themes/teal-night.json`, and the theme preference in `crates/app/src/commands/theme.rs`. "Retire our own completely" ends the `camcraft-theme/1` format. That is a breaking change: `feat!`, with "breaking" first in the cut notes.
- **Tab accents.** We have no tab table today. The ribbon groups and `op_tabs.rs` (135) would get one. The tab icons of #661 (its section 5) land with it.
- **Colour literals.** 51 `Color32` literals sit outside the theme and colour files. Each is a place the new tokens would not reach.

### Risks
1. **Licence:** no pin without the permission.
2. **Verdict colours:** gouge and rest are shown by colour in the viewport and on the traced stock. A remap that makes two classes look alike is a safety-display regression. The separation gate stays and takes the new palette.
3. **Merge conflicts:** renaming tokens touches 49 files and collides with every open UI PR. The rename goes last, in slices.
4. **Pixel goldens:** the 3 PNGs differ and are refreshed at the cut. The structural tests assert text, not colour, so few should move; that is a guess.

### Known and guessed
The line and site counts above are measured. "5-6 PRs" and "2-3k lines" are estimates. What would firm them up is the token map itself: which SolidCraft token feeds each of our 31, and which have none. It can be written from their source without building, once reading it for this purpose is covered by the permission.

### Proposed sub-issues, in build order

| # | Title | Done means | Effort | Areas | Depends on | Start |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | UI: no colour literals outside the token table | the 51 literal sites read a token; a guard test fails on a new literal | `effort:medium` | `area:ui` | - | today (ours either way) |
| 2 | Build: pin `solidcraft-color` and `solidcraft-theme` by rev | `cargo tree` shows one egui; a smoke test reads `Tokens::dark()`; licence text and the permission record are in `assets/ui/LICENSES.md` | `effort:medium` | `area:build`, `area:ui` | #658, the permission | waits on both; `needs-maintainer` |
| 3 | UI: our dark and light columns come from `solidcraft-theme` | `Tokens::DARK` and `LIGHT` are built from SolidCraft's tokens; both selectable; a test pins the map; no consumer file changes | `effort:medium` | `area:ui` | 2 | waits |
| 4 | UI: workspace tab table with accent ramps | CamCraft's tabs are installed as a `TabTable`; ribbon groups and operation tabs draw the accent; a test pins each tab's ramp | `effort:medium` | `area:ui` | 3; icons from #661 | waits |
| 5 | UI: colour-vision modes on `solidcraft-theme`, verdict palette stays ours | the mode switch drives SolidCraft's `set_vision`; verdict and move-kind colours pass the separation gate in every mode | `effort:high` | `area:ui`, `area:sim`, `accessibility` | 3 | waits |
| 6 | UI (breaking): retire `camcraft-theme/1` theme files | an old file is refused with a diagnostic that names it; the five files above and `teal-night.json` are gone; the preference falls back to dark | `effort:medium` | `area:ui` | 3; best after the kit's theme files are in (#655) | waits |
| 7 | Refactor: consumers read SolidCraft tokens directly (2 PRs: panes and tree, then pages) | the adapter struct is gone; the 233 references are moved; behaviour-neutral | `effort:medium` | `area:ui` | 3-6 | waits |

**Why `effort:high`:** a new dependency, three crates (root manifest, ui, the app's theme preference), a format retired, and the verdict colours. Row 5 is `effort:high` on its own because it changes how gouge and rest verdicts are shown.

**Labels:** this issue carries both `P2` and `P?`; one of them is for the maintainer to remove.

Maintainer (question dialog, 2026-11-12): this stays paused until SolidCraft answers the permission request (see #655). Filed from the breakdown above because they are useful either way: #1120 (no colour literals outside the token table).

Waits on the permission request to SolidCraft: https://github.com/tangency-labs/solidcraft/issues/15340 (posted 2026-11-12, tracked on #655). `solidcraft-theme` and the colour crate are among the crates the request names.
